name: @browz/mcp

tools.name: browz_profile_list
tools.description: List all browser profiles with their id, name, group, tags and last-used time. Start here to find a profile's id.

tools.name: browz_profile_create
tools.description: Create a profile. Each profile gets its own consistent, isolated fingerprint. Pass proxyId (from browz_proxy_list) to give it a proxy exit; without one it uses this machine's IP, which links it to every other unproxied profile.

proxyId.description: Pool id from browz_proxy_list. Strongly recommended.

archetype.description: macos | windows | linux — the platform the fingerprint imitates

engine.description: chromium (default, the Browz engine) | signed-chrome (the user's installed Google Chrome; needs proxyId, timezone and languages)

timezone.description: IANA timezone, e.g. Europe/Paris. Default: follows the proxy exit

languages.description: Accept-Language list, e.g. fr-FR,fr,en. Default: follows the proxy exit

tools.name: browz_profile_start
tools.description: Launch a profile's browser. Required before any page tool (navigate, snapshot, act, wait, screenshot). Next: browz_navigate. Returns the CDP debug port, cdpEndpoint and wsEndpoint.

headless.description: Override the agent's headless default for this launch (Browz engine only)

tools.name: browz_profile_stop
tools.description: Close a profile's browser cleanly, preserving its session.

tools.name: browz_profile_delete
tools.description: Move a profile to trash. Reversible — its proxy and browser data are kept until purged.

tools.name: browz_navigate
tools.description: Navigate a tab of a running profile to a URL and wait for load. http/https only. Next: browz_snapshot to see the page and get element refs.

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_evaluate
tools.description: Run a JavaScript expression in a running profile's page and return its value. A last resort: prefer browz_snapshot + browz_act, which send real input and leave no script trace.

expression.description: JavaScript expression; awaited if it returns a promise

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_screenshot
tools.description: PNG screenshot of a tab of a running profile, returned as an image. Use it to check what browz_snapshot cannot show (layout, images, canvas).

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_pages
tools.description: List the open tabs of a running profile (same as browz_tabs_list).

tools.name: browz_cookies_export
tools.description: Export a running profile's cookies.

tools.name: browz_profile_clone
tools.description: Copy a profile into a new one with a fresh, consistent fingerprint. The proxy is NOT copied: two profiles on one exit are linked. Returns the new profile.

tools.name: browz_tabs_list
tools.description: List the open tabs of a running profile with their targetId, title and url. Pass a targetId to the page tools to work in that tab.

tools.name: browz_tab_open
tools.description: Open a new tab in a running profile at an http(s) URL. Returns its targetId.

tools.name: browz_tab_close
tools.description: Close one tab of a running profile. The last tab cannot be closed; use browz_session_end.

tools.name: browz_snapshot
tools.description: Read a tab as an accessibility tree: roles, names, values and states, one element per line, plus the visible text. Interactive elements carry a ref like [e12] (pass "e12" to browz_act); a run of sibling links shares one line, `- links: "Home" [e5], "About" [e6]`, each link with its own ref. A ref stays valid while its element stays on the page; take a new snapshot after a navigation. The result reports its mode and estimated tokens; if the page does not fit maxTokens it falls back to a smaller mode and then truncates.

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

mode.description: compact (default): controls, headings, alerts and visible text. interactive: controls and headings only. full: every accessibility node

maxTokens.description: Token budget for the snapshot (about 4 characters a token). Default 10000

tools.name: browz_act
tools.description: Act on an element from the latest browz_snapshot with real input events: click, dblclick, hover, fill (replace a field's text), type (append), press (a key or chord such as Enter or Control+a), select (an option by value or label), check, uncheck, scroll, upload (set files on a file input, or on the input a button opens). Input is paced like a person: the pointer moves to the element, keys are typed one by one; human false sends it at once. Then browz_wait or browz_snapshot to see the result.

ref.description: Element ref from browz_snapshot, e.g. e12

key.description: Key or chord for press, e.g. Enter, Tab, Control+a

value.description: Option value or label for select

x.description: click/hover without a ref: viewport x. scroll without a ref: horizontal pixels

y.description: click/hover without a ref: viewport y. scroll without a ref: vertical pixels

files.description: upload: the files. Each is a name in the Browz data folder's agent-uploads folder, or a name plus its content as base64 in data (25 MiB in all)

human.description: Default true: pointer movement and typing paced like the profile's user. false: instant input

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_wait
tools.description: Wait until text appears, text disappears or the URL contains a string (or just wait timeMs). Returns matched=false on timeout rather than failing.

text.description: Wait until this text is on the page

textGone.description: Wait until this text is no longer on the page

urlContains.description: Wait until the URL contains this

timeMs.description: Fixed wait, when no condition is given

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_cookies_get
tools.description: Read a running profile's cookies, optionally only those for one domain (and its subdomains).

tools.name: browz_cookies_set
tools.description: Set cookies in a running profile. Each cookie needs name, value and domain (or url); path, expires, secure, httpOnly and sameSite are optional.

tools.name: browz_session_end
tools.description: End the session: close the profile's browser cleanly (its cookies and tabs are saved). With delete=true the profile is also moved to trash, where the person can restore it. With purge=true it is moved to trash and then deleted for good: use that for throwaway profiles you created for this task (an agent key may purge only profiles it created). For a throwaway task, browz_session_open (ephemeral) and browz_session_close wipe the profile for you.

delete.description: Also move the profile to trash (restorable)

purge.description: Also delete the profile for good: trash, then purge. Cannot be undone. An agent key may purge only profiles it created

tools.name: browz_group_list
tools.description: List profile groups.

tools.name: browz_proxy_list
tools.description: List the proxy pool. Passwords are never returned; use the returned id as proxyId when creating a profile.

tools.name: browz_running
tools.description: List profiles whose browser is currently running.

tools.name: browz_download_list
tools.description: List completed regular files in a profile's dedicated Downloads directory. Works while stopped or running; refresh if a running download changes identity.

tools.name: browz_download_read
tools.description: Read one bounded chunk of a listed download by opaque artifact id. Returns at most 65536 bytes as base64; use nextOffset until complete.

tools.name: browz_automation_read
tools.description: Read metadata-only durable automation operator state. Never exposes plans, secret values, worker claims, grants or effects.

tools.name: browz_automation_mutate
tools.description: Perform an allowlisted automation operator mutation. operationKey must be reused when retrying the same action.

tools.name: browz_bulk_read
tools.description: List/status/report metadata for durable profile metadata jobs.

tools.name: browz_bulk_submit
tools.description: Submit an allowlisted durable profile job with a stable idempotency key.

settings.description: Exact startupUrl/startupUrls assignment; empty clears profile-specific start pages

screen.description: Exact screen assignment: {mode:custom,value:{width,height}}, {mode:real} or {mode:auto} to clear

revision.description: Template revision the profiles are assigned to

extensionIds.description: Exact set1:/ext1: extension selectors, comma-separated, in precedence order; empty clears

proxyId.description: Opaque proxy-pool id; credentials are resolved only by the agent at dispatch

tools.name: browz_bulk_mutate
tools.description: Run one fenced durable batch or cancel a job. Reuse operationKey on retry.

tools.name: browz_bulk_report_prepare
tools.description: Prepare an immutable, restart-safe JSON or CSV artifact for a terminal durable profile job. Reuse operationKey for the exact request.

tools.name: browz_bulk_report_read
tools.description: Read one bounded path-free chunk from a prepared bulk report artifact. Returns at most 65536 bytes as base64; follow nextOffset until complete and verify digests.

tools.name: browz_session_open
tools.description: Open an agent session: an isolated profile of this task's own, with a consistent fingerprint, launched and ready for browz_navigate (use the returned profileId as id in page tools). mode ephemeral (default) gets a fresh profile that browz_session_close wipes (files, cookies, rows); mode persistent with an identity returns to that identity's profile, cookies and proxy. Parallel sessions never share storage. Refused with a clear message when the plan's concurrent-session limit is reached.

task.description: What this agent is doing (1-200 characters); shown in browz_session_list

mode.description: ephemeral (default): wiped on close; persistent: kept for a returning identity

identity.description: Persistent only: a stable name for the returning persona, e.g. shop-a/buyer-3 (letters, digits, - _ . : @ /)

proxy.description: none, pool (least-used pool proxy; a returning identity keeps its own), or {proxyId} from browz_proxy_list. Default: a returning identity's proxy, otherwise none

ttlMinutes.description: Ephemeral only: wipe the profile after this long even if never closed (default 1440)

launch.description: Launch the browser now (default true); false reserves the session and profile only

headless.description: Override the agent's headless default for this launch

archetype.description: New profiles only: macos | windows | linux

tools.name: browz_session_resume
tools.description: Resume an open agent session after its browser stopped or was killed: relaunches the same profile with its cookies and storage, or attaches if it is still running. Returns the launch endpoints.

headless.description: Override the agent's headless default for this launch

tools.name: browz_session_close
tools.description: Close an agent session and free its slot. Ephemeral: stops the browser and wipes the profile (no files or cookies left). Persistent: stops the browser and keeps the identity's profile for next time. Closing twice is harmless.

tools.name: browz_session_list
tools.description: List open agent sessions (state open or stopped, i.e. resumable) and the plan's concurrent-session limit.

tools.name: browz_request_human
tools.description: Hand the live profile to the person at the computer for a sign-in, 2FA code, CAPTCHA or other step you must not do yourself. Browz pauses automation, raises the profile window and notifies them; this call waits (with progress) until they click I'm done, cancel, or timeoutSec passes, then you continue in the same session. Never ask the person for passwords or codes and never use CAPTCHA-solving services. After it returns, take a new browz_snapshot.

reason.description: What the person should do, shown to them, e.g. 'Sign in to example.com'

kind.description: Detected from the page when omitted

timeoutSec.description: How long to wait for the person. Default 300

doneWhenUrlContains.description: Also finish as soon as a tab's URL contains this (e.g. /dashboard)

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

tools.name: browz_credential_list
tools.description: List the sign-ins the person stored for agents: id, label, a masked username hint, the sites each may be used on, whether a TOTP code is available, and extra field names. Never returns a password, code or seed. Pass id to see only those this profile may use.

id.description: Profile id: only credentials this profile may use. Omit for all

tools.name: browz_credential_fill
tools.description: Type one value of a stored credential (username, password, a fresh TOTP code, or a named extra field) into a field you found with browz_snapshot. Browz types it itself, paced like a person; the result says only that it was filled. Refused unless the tab (and any frame around the field) is on one of the credential's sites over https, and a password or code goes only into a password field (a code also into an autocomplete=one-time-code field). After a password or code is filled, browz_evaluate and browz_screenshot are refused on this profile until that tab loads another page; browz_snapshot keeps working and hides the value.

ref.description: The field's ref from browz_snapshot, e.g. e12

field.description: username, password, totp, or the name of one of the credential's extra fields

submit.description: Press Enter in the field after filling it. Default false

human.description: Type with the profile's human pacing (default true); false types at once

targetId.description: Tab to use: a targetId from browz_tabs_list. Default: the first tab

instructions: Browz gives each AI agent task its own isolated, fingerprint-protected browser profile, with its own proxy, cookies and storage. This server is running in offline mode because the Browz app is not installed here: the tools below are the real ones, and each call explains how to install Browz. We couldn't find the Browz app on this computer, so this tool can't run yet. Install Browz from https://gobrowz.com/download and open it: no account is needed for local use, and your agent can work while the app shows its sign-in screen. Then restart your MCP client so it starts this server again, and keep Browz open while your agent works. On macOS and Linux, once Browz is installed, you can also add it to a client in one line: curl -fsSL https://gobrowz.com/agents/install.sh | sh -s -- <client> (claude-code, claude-desktop, cursor or gemini-cli). If Browz is installed somewhere we don't look, set BROWZ_MCP to the path of its browz-mcp binary. Setup guide: https://gobrowz.com/docs/ai-agents
